summary.text: Jeffrey Hulum III is a Democrat and a member of the Mississippi House of Representatives for District 119, first elected in a 2022 special election. He is a retired U.S. Army sergeant major who served six combat deployments and founder of the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend. He won the March 10, 2026 Democratic primary for Mississippi's 4th District and cites the minimum wage, health care, and tariffs among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Hulum was born in Gulfport, Mississippi, and says in his Ballotpedia survey that he grew up in the Gaston Point community of West Gulfport.
He enlisted in the U.S. Army in 1996 and served 22 years, including six combat deployments to Kosovo, Iraq, and Afghanistan, retiring as a sergeant major; he says he received the Bronze Star.

He founded the nonprofit Extend A Hand, Help A Friend, which the Mississippi Free Press describes as working on food insecurity in Mississippi and which he says runs a mobile pantry, a free summer camp, and school-based food pantries and mentoring.

Hulum won the July 19, 2022 special general election for Mississippi House District 119, 67.5% to 32.5% over Gary Fredericks, and assumed office on August 5, 2022. In 2025-2026 he was assigned to the Marine Resources (vice chairman), Ports, Harbors and Airports, Military Affairs, Tourism, and Gaming committees.
In 2026 he won the March 10 Democratic primary for the 4th District with 57.7% of the vote over Paul Blackman and D. Ryan Grover.
